analysis.title: Trading up: An inside look at the growing trading card market
key_insights: Mizuho estimates the U.S. trading card market is a $10 billion to $20 billion opportunity, with annual sales above $1 billion at Target and Walmart combined.
Costco management has said trading cards carry some of the highest gross margins in its product assortment.

Demand has widened beyond baseball and other sports cards into Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, Star Wars and Disney character cards. Hasbro management called trading cards the 'hottest category in all of toys and games'.
eBay management has cited a 'long runway for secular growth' as sales accelerate across several categories.
Mizuho sees a real risk of a boom-and-bust cycle but does not think the dynamics that ended the Labubu and squishy dumpling fads are present in trading cards now.
Nostalgia supports demand: millennials with higher incomes are buying hobbies from their childhood, and Hasbro says the average Magic: The Gathering player is 35.

Multigenerational appeal (adults who grew up with Pokémon plus new young collectors, new athletes in sports cards) is why Mizuho thinks trading cards have more staying power than trend-driven collectibles.
Livestreamed breaks on Whatnot and eBay let viewers buy spots or shares in opened boxes. Whatnot raised $545 million at a reported $20 billion valuation earlier this year.

Fanatics (owner of Topps since 2022) runs programs such as the Topps MVP Buyback, which gives credit toward new purchases for eligible cards of award-winning players. Fanatics Fest drew more than 200,000 attendees in 2026, up from 125,000 in 2025.
PSA graded more than 19 million cards in 2025, up from 2 million five years earlier, and announced a $200 million investment in 2026 to expand operations, technology and workforce.
Hobby boxes with guaranteed autograph or relic cards are priced at $100-$1,000 or more. Hanger packs are the entry-level product with no guarantee.
Manufacturers now manage scarcity with limited parallels, numbered editions and one-of-one cards, after overproduction hurt value in the junk wax era of the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Coinbase signaled plans in 2026 to let users open trading-card packs on their phones, with each pull backed by a physical card that can be stored or shipped.
Mizuho expects momentum to continue into 2027 and beyond, driven by new releases, digital innovation and in-person events, and notes the category is increasingly viewed as an alternative asset class.

Risks named: speculative pricing, counterfeit cards, oversupply and changing consumer tastes. A PSA-graded 10 Pikachu Illustrator card sold for $16.5 million in 2026, a trading card auction record, which Mizuho calls froth at the high end but not pervasive.

sector_views.rationale: Mizuho sees a $10-20 billion U.S. market with multigenerational demand, expanding platforms and expected momentum into 2027 and beyond, while noting boom-and-bust risk.

earnings_insights: Hasbro management described trading cards as the 'hottest category in all of toys and games' (management commentary, no figures given).
eBay management referenced a 'long runway for secular growth' amid accelerating sales across several categories (management commentary, no figures given).
Costco management said trading cards generate some of the highest gross margins in its assortment (no figure given).
crypto_views: Coinbase signaled plans in 2026 to let users open trading-card packs on their phones, with each pull backed by a physical card that could be stored or shipped, which Mizuho describes as a potential convergence of digital commerce, physical assets and collecting.
risk_factors: Speculative pricing in rare cards, including the $16.5 million Pikachu Illustrator sale.
Oversupply, as in the junk wax era of the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Changing consumer tastes and fad risk, as with Labubus and squishy dumplings.
Participation in the market does not guarantee success for every business.

tension_points.bull_case: Nostalgia-driven millennial spending, multigenerational appeal, livestream platforms, PSA grading growth (19 million cards in 2025) and Fanatics Fest attendance of 200,000+ support momentum into 2027 and beyond.
tension_points.bear_case: Speculative pricing, counterfeits, oversupply and changing tastes could undermine parts of the market, with froth at the high end such as the $16.5 million Pikachu Illustrator sale.

theme_stances.key_argument: Nostalgia, innovation and a diverse ecosystem give trading cards staying power unlike short-lived fads.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect momentum to continue into 2027 and beyond
